projectTitle: note-zephyr: Zephyr module for Blues Notecard
description: Zephyr RTOS west module for using a Blues Notecard over I2C or UART. It wraps the note-c library with Zephyr transports selected by devicetree and registers heap, timing, mutex, and logging hooks at boot, so applications call the note-c API directly. Configured with Kconfig (CONFIG_BLUES_NOTECARD). Includes blinky, message queue, binary transfer, and shell examples.
rules: Add note-zephyr to your west.yml manifest with `submodules: true`; the module needs its note-c submodule.
Enable the module in prj.conf with CONFIG_NEWLIB_LIBC=y and CONFIG_BLUES_NOTECARD=y. note-c allocates from its own heap, sized by CONFIG_BLUES_NOTECARD_HOOKS_HEAP_SIZE (default 16384 bytes).
Select I2C or UART in devicetree, not code: add a node with compatible = "blues,notecard" under an I2C bus (reg = <0x17>) or a UART, as in examples/overlays/i2c.overlay and uart.overlay.

The module registers note-c's memory, timing, mutex, logging and transport hooks at boot; don't call NoteSetFn(), NoteSetFnI2C() or NoteSetFnSerial(). Include <note.h> and call NoteNewRequest() and NoteRequest().
Set the ProductUID with CONFIG_BLUES_NOTEHUB_PRODUCT_UID in prj.conf and pass it as the "product" argument of hub.set.
NoteRequest() and NoteRequestResponse() free the request; check each response with NoteResponseError() and free it with NoteDeleteResponse().
Copy Notecard request and argument names exactly from the Notecard API reference; do not invent requests, arguments, or response fields.
When the Blues Expert MCP server is connected, check generated Notecard JSON requests with its api_validate tool before using them.
